h1: Warm water appears at a cold tap
title: Warm water appears at a cold tap | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand warm water appears at a cold tap. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Unexpected warm cold-water delivery needs the affected outlets and system arrangement assessed; do not assume one universal cylinder cause.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: Heat transfer, a mixing fault or a cross-connection can be among the conditions an engineer investigates. The symptom history matters: one tap, several outlets and sustained warming do not mean the same thing.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Note whether the water clears quickly, whether unused outlets are involved and if plumbing work occurred recently. Keep hygiene and scalding risks in view rather than changing cylinder controls yourself.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can warm cold-water delivery be diagnosed just from the cylinder brand?
faqs.answer: No. Outlet behaviour, mixing arrangements, pipework and temperature history must be assessed; the brand alone does not identify the cause.
